fi-paracirrhites-arcatus.title: Arc-Eye Hawkfish
fi-paracirrhites-arcatus.summary: A hawkfish named for the arc-shaped mark behind its eye. A predator of small crustaceans and fish.
rows: About 8 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 20 cm (7.9 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. Eats crabs, shrimp and small fish
Carnivore. A variety of marine meats
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Hawaiian, Line and Mangaréva islands, north to southern Japan, south to Australia and Rapa

fi-neocirrhites-armatus.title: Flame Hawkfish
fi-neocirrhites-armatus.summary: A bright scarlet hawkfish with dark eye rings from the western and central Pacific. It perches in branching coral and watches for prey.
rows: About 4 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 9 cm (3.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: frozen mysis shrimp, chopped marine meats, frozen carnivore preparations, live shrimp, marine pellets, marine flakes
Pacific Ocean: Ryukyu Islands to the Line Islands and Mangaréva, south to the Great Barrier Reef and the Austral Islands; Caroline, Mariana
notes: Corals are safe, but it hunts crustaceans: small shrimp, hermit and other small crabs, snails and feather dusters are at risk.

fi-cyprinocirrhites-polyactis.title: Lyretail Hawkfish (Swallowtail Hawkfish)
fi-cyprinocirrhites-polyactis.summary: An unusual hawkfish with a forked, lyre-shaped tail and a short snout, red to orange in color. Unlike most hawkfish it often swims up in the water to feed on plankton.
rows: About 5.9 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: frozen mysis shrimp, chopped shrimp, scallop, krill, squid, fish flesh, frozen plankton, carnivore pellets
Indo-West Pacific: East Africa south to the southeast coast of South Africa and east to Tonga, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia
notes: Leaves corals alone; shrimp, crabs and much smaller fish may be eaten.
